# Khandhavibhaṅga (Vb 1)

**ID:** Vb 1
**Section:** Vibhaṅga (vb)
**Collection:** Abhidhamma
**Title (Pali):** Khandhavibhaṅga
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/abh02m.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Khandhavibhaṅga* ("Analysis of the Aggregates") constitutes the opening chapter of the *Vibhaṅga*, the second treatise of the Theravāda Abhidhamma Piṭaka [Hazra 1994; Williams 2005]. As with many chapters of the work, it is structured into three consecutive sections: a discourse analysis (*suttanta-bhājaniya*), an Abhidhamma analysis (*abhidhamma-bhājaniya*), and an interrogation section (*pañhapucchaka*) [Williams 2005].

The *suttanta-bhājaniya* (Vibh 1–12) expounds the five aggregates (*pañcakkhandhā*—corporeality, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness) using the canonical formula that distributes each aggregate across an elevenfold classification: past, future, or present; internal or external; gross or subtle; inferior or superior; and far or near [Bodhi 2003; Nyanatiloka 1938; Williams 2005]. The *abhidhamma-bhājaniya* treats each aggregate systematically by dissecting it into multiple numerical permutations (twofold, threefold, and fourfold divisions) aligned with the Abhidhamma matrix (*mātikā*), yielding extensive permutations [Williams 2005]. The concluding *pañhapucchaka* presents a catechism of questions and answers establishing how the aggregates correlate with the Abhidhamma triplets (*tika*) and couplets (*duka*) [Williams 2005]. The text has a direct counterpart in the *Khandhasaṃyutta* of the *Saṃyutta Nikāya* [Bodhi 2003], and its expository method closely resembles sections of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* [Nyanatiloka 1938].

 DharmaNexus computational analysis highlights extensive Pali-internal text reuse (over 24,000 matching passages across 347 texts), most prominently with subsequent *Vibhaṅga* chapters—such as the *Āyatanavibhaṅga* (Vb 2), *Dhātuvibhaṅga* (Vb 3), and *Indriyavibhaṅga* (Vb 5)—as well as the *Abhidhammamātikā*, the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī*, various treatises of the *Paṭṭhāna*, and the commentary *Vibhaṅga-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns passages of the text with Northern Abhidharma and scholastic works analyzing the aggregates, including the Tibetan *Karmaprajñapti* (D4088), the *Saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtaviniścaya* (D3897), the *Abhidharmakośabhāṣya* (D4090), and Sanskrit works such as Asaṅga's *Abhidharmasamuccaya* and Sthiramati's *Pañcaskandhakavibhāṣā* [DharmaNexus].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Text reuse within the Pali corpus (DharmaNexus): Āyatanavibhaṅga (Vb 2) (§526.12–530.1 ↔ §62.12–66.1); Abhidhammamātikāpāḷi (Tika Abh09t) (§402.10–402.21 ↔ §96_3–96_9); Dhātuvibhaṅga (Vb 3) (§532.1–538.1 ↔ §92.2–101.1); Indriyavibhaṅga (Vb 5) (§533.6–534.5_2 ↔ §75.7–77.6); Ñāṇavibhaṅga (Vb 16) (§402.10–402.21 ↔ §88.1–97.1); Paṭiccasamuppādavibhaṅga (Vb 6) (§50.2_1–51.1 ↔ §8.2–9.1); Mātikā (Ds 2.2.2) (§60.1–68.3 ↔ §64.7–115.2); Saccavibhaṅga (Vb 4) (§534.6–535.19 ↔ §141.25–142.22)
- Cross-language matches (DharmaNexus): ལས་གདགས་པ། (karmaprajñapti) (D4088) [bo]; BO_K10_Dx_H0290 [bo]; འདུས་བྱས་དང་འདུས་མ་བྱས་རྣམ་པར་ངེས་པ་ཞེས་བྱ་བ། (saṃskṛtāsaṃskṛtaviniścaya-nāma) (D3897) [bo]; རྣལ་འབྱོར་སྤྱོད་པའི་ས། (yogācārabhūmi) (D4035) [bo]; Yogācārabhūmi: Śrāvakabhūmi (SA_T06_srabhu_u) [sa]; Sthiramati (vibhāṣā/commentary); on Vasubandhu's root Pañcaskandhaka: Pañcaskandhakavibhāṣā (SA_T06_pskvbhu) [sa]; Arthaviniścayasūtra (SA_K10_bsu005_u) [sa]; Asaṅga: Abhidharmasamuccaya (SA_T06_asabhs_u) [sa]
- [Bodhi 2003] Bhikkhu Bodhi, The Connected Discourses of the Buddha: A New Translation of the Samyutta Nikaya (2003) — Identifies Khandhavibhaṅga as having counterparts in the Saṃyutta Nikāya and notes its elevenfold aggregate analysis at Vibh 1–12
- [DharmaNexus] DharmaNexus database — Provides data on internal Pali text reuse and cross-language alignments with Sanskrit and Tibetan treatises
- [Hazra 1994] Kanai Lal Hazra, Pali Language and Literature (1994) — Confirms Khandhavibhaṅga as the first of eighteen chapters of the Vibhaṅga
- [Nyanatiloka 1938] Nyanatiloka Mahāthera, Guide Through the Abhidhamma Pitaka (1938) — Outlines the five groups and notes textual affinities between the Vibhaṅga and the Paṭisambhidāmagga
- [Williams 2005] Paul Williams (ed.), Buddhism: Critical Concepts in Religious Studies, Vol. IV (2005) — Details the tripartite structure (suttanta-bhājaniya, abhidhamma-bhājaniya, and pañhapucchaka) and analytical methods of the Khandhavibhaṅga
